declared.text: kT declares AOI-2226 refractive-index matching and independently switchable clear/glare/dark plus visible/NIR modulation. NOT demonstrated at full scale. Zero numeric optical/IR cooling performance credited; worst Venus solar aperture heat explicitly included. Transparent dome and AOI thermal expansion/differential heat flux remain OPEN.
declared.as: Zero quantified thermal attenuation or dynamic optical performance credited. Worst-case glazing heat counted.

declared.text: Torch heat package (kT, 2026-10-25): each pellet is wrapped in a shell of remass that soaks up the burn and leaves as exhaust. The shell must let no more than ~358 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow (the reactor face's 10 MW/m2 limit); the design value is 180 ppm. With the model's other assumptions (torch/torch_heat_inputs.json: light 40% of fusion energy; He3-rich, spin-polarised fuel with 0.76% neutrons, 85% absorbed by the shell; plume contact 1e-4 of charged energy; coil shield transmission 1e-3), 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils at 12.6 TW of fusion. These are assumptions, not results. Replaces v0.5.1's 387 MW (34 ppm) torch-leak gap.
declared.as: v0.5.2 torch heat package (kT chose the package and 1,750 K fins on 2026-10-25 and accepted this wording the same day): the remass shell lets no more than ~360 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow; design value 180 ppm; with the heat model's other assumptions 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils.

declared.text: Hot fins run for life at 1750 K. Lithium heat pipes have run in lab tests to ~1,500 K and briefly ~1,800 K; years at 1750 K with burn cycling and neutron exposure is an engineering extrapolation (a technology milestone), not new physics. Fallback: 1,500 K fins, ~49 m span, ~30 t, still inside the reserve.
declared.as: kT: "Let's go 1750." Hot fins at 1,750 K, recorded as an engineering extrapolation (technology milestone), with 1,500 K fins as the fallback.

declared.text: Plant electrical: Metric HARD at a 1300 K reject temperature needs 34.8 MW of cryo-chain electrical power, against canon's 23.9 MW at 900 K. The relational plant must supply this (canon amendment), or the cryo chain must reject through a 900 K loop.
declared.as: canon states the relational plant supplies ~34.8 MW for Metric HARD at a 1,300 K reject temperature. Option not taken: a 900 K loop for the cryo chain.

declared.text: At worst-case sunlight, the open crown adds ~100 kW of solar heating to habitat. In heat-pump-failed or cold-running passive backup the 16 Strata gores MUST CLOSE; clear/glare/dark AOI states may not be credited as heat rejection or solar exclusion. Solar absorption/IR-band partition and AOI switching performance are not physically qualified.
declared.as: Model-derived operating restriction: active open-crown worst Venus sun creates ~100kW load; heat pump failed requires closure. Physical controls remain unqualified.

declared.text: Cold running (rev 7, F5 provisional item F5-TE-01): the tunable flanks drop from emissivity 0.85 to 0.1, so at the same skin temperature they radiate 12% as much. Heat is held, not removed: habitat heat 58.1 kW (x1.25), plus plant standby 10.0 kW and cryo standby 10.0 kW, less 7.1 kW still leaking through 177 m2 of low-e skin at 290 K warms the 50 t of protected water by 15 K in about 12.3 h (ideal no-standby ceiling 17.1 h). ENGINEERING_ASSUMPTION (screening placeholders 10+10 kW, NOT sourced or qualified); editable, replace with measured/engineering budget. Then the ship must open the strakes or switch the flanks back to normal. Detailed load-cycle variation, cryo plant duty, tank thermal coupling, and reserve storage remain open. The metallic look in the viewer is a proposed optical property.
declared.as: Provisional ~17.09h ideal cap before plant and cryo standby; 10+10 kW editable illustrative loads yield a shorter window; physical heat budget OPEN

notes: Habitat heat 146.6 kW for 10 people; heat pump to 1300 K needs 1021 kW (Carnot fraction 0.5).
Torch burns: strakes open to 4.0 m (73 MW); full 24 m span (387 MW) is no longer needed for the torch. At 4.0 m they shine 1.46 MW onto the hull coating.

Torch heat model (torch/, non-governing): same 11.36 TW jet from 12.6 TW of fusion, pulsed at about 1-10 Hz (0.3-3 kt per pulse). Light escape the face can take: ~358 ppm; model 180 ppm. Hot-fin capacity is computed here with certify's own 2D view factor; torch/fin_layout.py (numpy, 3.0 m body) gives a slightly higher figure.

declared.text: Galactic cosmic rays: at 2026 free-space rates (1.8 mSv/day, ~657 mSv/yr) a crew member reaches NASA's 600 mSv career limit after ~333 days in deep space. declared_for_kT.text: Torch heat package (kT, 2026-10-25): each pellet is wrapped in a shell of remass that soaks up the burn and leaves as exhaust. The shell must let no more than ~358 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow (the reactor face's 10 MW/m2 limit); the design value is 180 ppm. With the model's other assumptions (torch/torch_heat_inputs.json: light 40% of fusion energy; He3-rich, spin-polarised fuel with 0.76% neutrons, 85% absorbed by the shell; plume contact 1e-4 of charged energy; coil shield transmission 1e-3), 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils at 12.6 TW of fusion. These are assumptions, not results. Replaces v0.5.1's 387 MW (34 ppm) torch-leak gap.
declared_for_kT.as: v0.5.2 torch heat package (kT chose the package and 1,750 K fins on 2026-10-25 and accepted this wording the same day): the remass shell lets no more than ~360 ppm of the burn's energy escape as light, counting its own glow; design value 180 ppm; with the heat model's other assumptions 1.40 GW reaches hot structure and 0.48 MW the magnet coils.
